verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2025, assessment updated 11 Jun 2025): same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, gender-marker changes on documents are prohibited, trans people cannot adopt or foster, trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, and no legislation prohibits SOGI-based discrimination in housing, healthcare or employment. Publicly 'promoting' non-heterosexual relationships or gender transition is an administrative offence (fines or detention up to 15 days; repeat offences can become criminal, up to 4 years), the 2023 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement criminalises support/activity, and at least 139 people were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws 2022-2024. Assesses LGB people generally face no real risk of state persecution on orientation alone, except in the North Caucasus — a zone that does not include Altai Krai; this is the national baseline the record stands assessed at.
verdicts.note: national-framework reporting; record assessed at national score; no region-specific source

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (30 Jun 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions over alleged participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols (about 98 administrative); since January 2024, 81 people in 98 court cases were found guilty of administrative offences under article 20.3 for displaying symbols such as the rainbow flag, and between Jan 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges for alleged participation — one died by suicide in pretrial detention, two were sentenced to prison, 17 cases pending or unknown. On 15 May 2025 investigators charged three staff of two publishing houses under article 282.2 with running an 'extremist organisation' over selling fiction exploring LGBT themes; they face up to 12 years in prison. National enforcement regime applying equally in Altai Krai; no Altai Krai-specific case is reported in the piece.
verdicts.note: national-framework reporting; record assessed at national score; no region-specific source
